MOTIVATION_01: To make my undergraduate experience complete
PRIOR_05:
In my earlier research experiences, I typically worked within a defined structure. The projects already had established frameworks, research questions, and clear expectations. My role was to contribute to ongoing work, follow existing methodologies, and support goals that had largely been set before I joined.
Discovery Hubs, on the other hand, encouraged a far more exploratory approach. Instead of entering a predetermined project, I was invited to identify questions that genuinely interested me, pursue emerging ideas, and take intellectual risks. The emphasis was not only on producing results, but on curiosity, experimentation, and discovery. This shift made the research feel much more self-directed and creative.
PRIOR_06: Reaching out directly to a professor
PRIOR_07: I chose the Discovery Hubs because they offered something that traditional research avenues often do not: a space where exploration, creativity, and student-driven inquiry are not only allowed but encouraged. Unlike more formal research programs where projects are predefined and roles are narrowly structured, the Discovery Hubs gave me the freedom to pursue ideas that genuinely interested me and the support to develop them in meaningful ways.
INTEREST_02: The freedom to explore ideas in the Hubs introduced me to topics I might never have encountered through traditional coursework. Pursuing those interests helped me understand what kinds of questions energize me and what environments I thrive in. This has guided me toward more intentional academic choices and helped clarify the types of roles I want to pursue in the future.
